Static Voltage Stability Based Maximum Integration
Ratio of Distributed Renewable Energy in
Distribution Power System
Mosi Liu*, Zhiyuan Sun, Jinzhao Li,and Kun Zheng
Electric Power Research Institute of Guangxi Power Grid Co., Ltd., Nanning 530023, China
*Corresponding author's e-mail: lmosi@qq.com
Abstract. Distributed renewable energy source (DREs) is an
effective supplement to traditional centralized power generation
systems. However, how to allocate the DREs and how to evaluate
the maximum integration ratio of DREs are the two main
obstacles hindering the development of DREs. To tackle these
problems, this paper proposes a novel optimal allocation method
for DREs in distribution power systems with static voltage
s t a b i l i t y a s t h e c o n s t r a i n t . B a s e d o n t h e o p t i m a l a l l o c a t i o n
method, one maximum integration ratio of DREs in the
distribution power system is studied. The theoretical analysis and
case studies show the effectiveness of the proposed allocation and
evaluation methods of DREs. Moreover, the proposed allocation
method of DREs can achieve high efficiency and low power loss.
Keywords: distributed renewable energy source;static voltage
stability;distribution power system;optimal allocation method
I. Introduction
Distributed renewable energy source (DREs) is an
effective supplement to traditional centralized power
generation systems. The combined and complementary power
generation model of traditional centralized power generation
and DREs has the functions of achieving green development,
reducing transmission losses, saving investment, and
improving system reliability. It breaks the shortcomings of
high pollution and low reliability of traditional centralized
power supply systems, improves energy utilization efficiency,
and flexibly distributes location-allocation, satisfying the
characteristics of existing resource distribution and the
demand for decentralized power supply [1-2].
However, the dynamic reactive power support capability
of renewable energy units is weak [3]. With the rapid increase
in the proportion of renewable energy, the system voltage
support capability drops sharply, and the problem of voltage
stability is prominent. The static voltage stability can reflect
the voltage stability level of the system to a certain extent.
Therefore, studying the static voltage stability and its margin
of the new energy multi-station transmission system is of great
significance for the safe and stable operation of the system [4].
O n e o f t h e m a i n f a c t o r s l i m i t i n g t h e D R E s l e v e l i s t h e
voltage exceeding the limit caused by the reverse power flow
caused by the renewable energy access. A simple solution is to
reduce the voltage setting of the substation or use an automatic
voltage controller (AVC) on the feeder. However, the access
capacity and location of DREs are different, so the allocation
of AVC or dynamic reactive power compensator is
complicated. Besides, the investment of the extra AVC
equipment in each accession node is high. Moreover, the
voltage distribution of the whole feeder cannot be guaranteed
in an acceptable range by just the on-load tap-changer due to
the dynamic changes in the renewable energy output. In [5],
an approach to find suitable sites for integrating DREs on the
basis of maximum power that can be injected at these sites
without violating transmission network constraints is proposed,
but the approach is a little complicated. In [6], a technique for
finding the optimal locations and sizes of (RESs) in electric
power systems is proposed by using oscillatory particle swarm
optimization. However, the static voltage constraint is not
fully considered in these available studies.
Therefore, this paper intends to study the maximum
integration of DREs in the distribution power system while
considering static voltage stability. The main contributions of
this paper are as follows:
1) the optimal allocation method of DREs in the
distribution power system is proposed.
2) the maximum integration ratio of DREs with static
voltage stability as a constraint is proposed.
II. Static voltage stability of distribution power system
The basic unit of the distribution power system is the
feeder. The first end of the feeder is connected to the high-
voltage distribution network through a high-voltage step-down
transformer, and the end is connected to the user through a
low-voltage step-down transformer. The voltage level of most
feeder lines in China is 10 kV, and the lines on each feeder are
distributed in a tree shape, connected to several distribution
transformers through a radial network.

DREs

nodes with a radial structure can be divided into two parts: one
is the last power load node, and the remaining part can be seen
as an equivalent source part. Therefore, the theory of the
distribution system with two DREs integration is applicable to
that with N DREs.

V. Conclusion and future work
The allocation value of DREs in distribution with a radial
network has a great influence on the static voltage of the
distribution nodes. An unreasonable allocation value of DREs
in distribution will cause some nodes to exceed the static
voltage limits and result in a large power transmission loss.
Hence, this paper proposes a novel optimal allocation method
for DREs in a distribution power system with static voltage
stability as the constraint. Based on the optimal allocation
method, one maximum integration ratio of DREs in the
distribution power system is studied. Through the theoretical
analysis and simulation verification, it can be concluded that
the optimal allocation value of DREs should be equal to the
power load except for the node closest to the source node (the
substation). Compared to other allocation methods of DREs in
distribution, this allocation method can avoid power backflow
except for the node closest to the source node, thereby
preventing some remote nodes from exceeding the voltage
limit and reducing the power losses caused by line impedance
during the transmission.
The impact of the reactive power on the allocation method
suitable for the distribution with a ring network will be studied
in further work.
